articles.title: Celulares são apreendidos em presídio no interior do Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Polícia Penal apreendeu aparelhos entre esse sábado (31) e domingo (1º) na Unidade Penal Evaristo de Morais, em Sena Madureira.
articles.summary: Polícia Penal apreendeu aparelhos entre esse sábado (31) e domingo (1º) na Unidade Penal Evaristo de Morais, em Sena Madureira.
articles.body:
No segundo embrulho, arremessado por cima da muralha neste domingo (1º), foram encontrados oito celulares e três carregadores — Foto: Arquivo/Iapen-AC

Cerca de 11 aparelhos celulares foram apreendidos entre esse sábado (31) e domingo (1º), na Unidade Penal Evaristo de Morais, em Sena Madureira , no interior do Acre.

Segundo o Instituto de Administração Penitenciária do Acre (Iapen-AC), a primeira apreensão ocorreu nesse sábado (31), quando os policiais penais conseguiram interceptar e apreender o pacote com os aparelhos arremessados por um homem da BR-364 ao pátio de banho de sol, na unidade prisional. No interior do embrulho foram encontrados três aparelhos e um fone de ouvido.

A segunda apreensão ocorreu na madrugada deste domingo (1º), após uma nova tentativa de introduzir aparelhos de telefone na unidade. De acordo com o instituto, os policiais penais viram quando um indivíduo, que não foi identificado, arremessou um embrulho por cima da muralha de segurança.

Conforme o Iapen-AC, os agentes conseguiram interceptar e apreender o material. Após averiguação do pacote, foram contabilizados oito aparelhos celulares e três carregadores. Os objetos são de uso proibido pelos custodiados.

Todos os materiais apreendidos foram recolhidos e encaminhados à direção do presídio para a confecção do boletim de ocorrência interno, para a instauração de Procedimento Administrativo Disciplinar (PAD) e comunicação ao Juízo da Vara de Execuções Penais, além da autoridade policial para apuração do crime.

No interior do embrulho do primeiro arremesso, os agentes encontraram três aparelhos de celular e um fone de ouvido — Foto: Arquivo/Iapen-AC

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3080 acumula e prêmio vai a R$ 46 milhões; confira números | G1
articles.standfirst: O prêmio para o ganhador da edição deste domingo era de R$ 40,7 milhões.
articles.summary: O prêmio para o ganhador da edição deste domingo era de R$ 40,7 milhões.
articles.body:
O sorteio do concurso 3.080 da Mega-Sena foi realizado na manhã deste domingo (1º), em São Paulo. O prêmio para as apostas que acertassem as seis dezenas era de R$ 40,7 milhões . No entanto, ninguém levou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou para R$ 46 milhões .

Veja os números sorteados: 13 - 17 - 28 - 29 - 39 - 58

5 acertos: 29 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 38.878,66

4 acertos: 3.133 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 514,10

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

Resultado do concurso 3080 da Mega-Sena. — Foto: Reprodução/Caixa

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e o tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Incêndio atinge food truck na Área Hospitalar, em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Bombeiros utilizaram cerca de mil litros de água para combater as chamas e fazer o rescaldo. Segundo o proprietário, fogo começou em uma churrasqueira instalada no caminhão de lanches.
articles.summary: Segundo o proprietário, fogo começou em uma churrasqueira instalada no caminhão de lanches
articles.body:
Food Truck 'Toro Beer Espetos e Chopp Artesanal' pegou fogo neste domingo (1º) em BH — Foto: Lucas Franco/TV Globo

Um food truck pegou fogo na Praça Hugo Werneck, no bairro Santa Efigênia, na Região Centro-Sul de Belo Horizonte , na manhã deste domingo (1º). Ninguém ficou ferido.

Segundo o proprietário do estabelecimento, o incêndio começou em uma churrasqueira instalada no caminhão de lanches.

Uma equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros, que passava pelo local no momento do acidente, prestou os primeiros socorros. Em seguida, outra viatura de combate a incêndio também deslocou.

Os militares retiraram botijões de gás e utilizaram aproximadamente mil litros de água para controlar as chamas e realizar o trabalho de rescaldo.

Ao g1 , o proprietário do estabelecimento contou que o veículo não possui seguro e que os prejuízos ainda serão calculados.

Um reboque deve retirar o food truck do local neste domingo (1º). A previsão é que outro seja instalado na praça nesta segunda-feira (2), para que as vendas sejam retomadas.

articles.title: Russa em João Pessoa: 'na Rússia não existe veneração às grávidas'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Custos de procedimentos e tratamento dos médicos atraem gestantes para a capital paraibana. Dados federais apontam que cerca de 60 mil cidadãos da Rússia entraram no Brasil entre março de 2022 e o fim de 2025.
articles.summary: A busca por parto humanizado em João Pessoa atrai gestantes russas que trocam Moscou pela Paraíba em busca de acolhimento médico e custos acessíveis no Brasil.
articles.body:
Viktoriia Baskakova que escolheu João Pessoa para ter filhos disse que busca por parto humanizado motivou decisão. Antes de morar na capital paraibana, ela viveu em Moscou, na Argentina e em outros estados brasileiros.

“Na Rússia não existe essa veneração às grávidas, como tem aqui. Ter um acompanhante no parto, bem, geralmente custa muito caro, mas além disso tem muitos obstáculos e os médicos não são muito a favor. E eu diria que lá tem intervenções mais brutais”, relatou.

João Pessoa tem sido uma das cidades escolhidas por gestantes russas para o nascimento dos seus filhos. De acordo com as mulheres, a escolha parte de uma busca por atendimento humanizado e acolhimento durante a gestação, não muito comum em seu país de origem.

O interesse na capital tem incentivado as mulheres a realizarem um processo migratório de quase 10 mil quilômetros de Moscou, capital da Rússia, até a Paraíba. É o caso de Viktoriia Baskakova, que morou em Moscou, na Argentina e em outros estados brasileiros antes de se mudar para João Pessoa.

“Conhecemos a cidade, vimos as praias, depois nos demos bem com o clima. Foi a primeira vez na vida que eu e meu marido concordamos plenamente que íamos ficar por aqui mesmo e construir a vida justamente aqui”, contou.

Família de russos se mudam para João Pessoa, Paraíba — Foto: Reprodução TV Cabo Branco.

Desde que se mudou para a Paraíba, Viktoriia teve uma filha e está grávida do quinto filho. Segundo ela, as diferenças no tratamento às gestantes e os custos dos serviços de saúde influenciaram sua decisão de permanecer no Brasil.

A percepção de Viktoriia não representa um caso isolado. De acordo com o ginecologista e obstetra, Guilherme Carvalho, o processo de migração de gestantes russas se intensificou a aproximadamente um ano e meio.

“Inicialmente eu achava que era mais pela cidade, João Pessoa está recebendo muitos turistas estrangeiros, mas pontualmente eu comecei a perceber, nesse ano, uma demanda muito grande de russos especificamente. Porque eu já tinha atendido italiana, já tinha atendido ucraniana, já tinha atendido portuguesa. Atualmente eu estou fazendo um pré-natal de 12 pacientes russrs”, disse.

Gestantes russas escolhem João Pessoa para o nascimento dos filhos — Foto: Reprodução TV Cabo Branco.

Para facilitar a comunicação durante as consultas, as gestantes contam com tradutoras ou plataformas de tradução.

“A grande maioria, elas vão com uma tradutora, uma pessoa para estar ali traduzindo e para a comunicação fluir melhor, mas outras a gente acaba usando realmente o tradutor (...) A gente, ao longo dos acompanhamentos, da vinculação, a gente vai ganhando uma intimidade e vai também aprendendo junto com eles e facilitando essa conversa”, explicou a doula Thayana Jovino.

O médico também utiliza equipamentos que traduzem as conversas em tempo real. Prontuários, receitas e materiais com orientações sobre a gravidez são adaptados para o russo.

“Eu tenho um equipamento que ele me ajuda muito porque ele, eu falo em português e elas escutam em russo, elas falam em russo e eu escuto em português. Nas prescrições, eu tento também sempre adaptar. Assim como alguns materiais que a gente dá sobre os cuidados na gravidez. Então, as meninas se adaptam, colocam em russo para que elas tenham esse acolhimento e que essa linguagem também fique mais fácil”, complementou.

A escolha pelo Brasil também ocorre em um contexto mais amplo de imigração russa. Dados do governo federal apontam que cerca de 60 mil cidadãos russos entraram no país entre março de 2022 e os últimos meses de 2025. Entre 2024 e 2025, outras 1.094 pessoas de origem russa obtiveram a cidadania brasileira.

O contexto considera uma questão geopolítica em que a imigração russa não acontece com facilidade para países vizinhos, segundo a doutora em Relações Internacionais Leila Bijos. Outro ponto é com relação às restrições em relação aos procedimentos médicos, como no caso de partos cirúrgicos, por meio de cesáreas;

“A s russas sentem falta de conversar, de trocar ideias , porque a mãe fica muito insegura na gestação, principalmente nos últimos meses. Então , isso no Brasil é importantíssimo, porque os nossos médicos são amigos ”, disse a especialista.

Diante da sua experiência como imigrante, Viktoriia se dedicou ao acolhimento de gestantes distantes de seu país de origem. Atualmente, ela atua como doula e cria os filhos na capital paraibana.

“É muito necessário esse apoio às mulheres em geral, quando estão em um país diferente, em um lugar bem incompreensível. Eu tento passar para os meus filhos essa vivência positiva, mostrar as vantagens de viver aqui para os meus filhos mais velhos. Como uma já nasceu e a outra vai nascer aqui logo, elas vão crescer nessa cultura, já vão fazer parte dessa sociedade naturalmente e, na minha visão, vai ser até mais fácil para elas, de certa forma”, concluiu.

Viktoriia Baskakova, russa que escolheu João Pessoa para nascimento dos filhos — Foto: Reprodução TV Cabo Branco.

articles.title: Enem 2026 na Paraíba: mulheres são 60% dos inscritos no estado | G1
articles.standfirst: Número de participantes do sexo feminino passou de 82,7 mil em 2025 para 84,1 mil neste ano. Ao todo, o estado tem cerca de 140,7 mil inscritos no exame.
articles.summary: O Enem 2026 na Paraíba registra 140,7 mil inscritos, com destaque para o público feminino e provas marcadas para os dias 8 e 15 de novembro em todo o estado.
articles.body:
2º dia de aplicação do Enem 2025. — Foto: Angelo Miguel/MEC e Bruna Araújo/MEC.

As mulheres representam aproximadamente 60% dos inscritos no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026 na Paraíba, de acordo com dados do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep). Ao todo, são 84.147 participantes do sexo feminino, enquanto o número total de inscritos no estado chega a cerca de 140,7 mil.

Em 2025, o número de mulheres inscritas foi de 82.787, o equivalente a 58,28% do total de participantes. Na comparação entre os dois anos, houve um aumento de 1.360 inscrições femininas, o que representa um crescimento de aproximadamente 1,64% no número de mulheres participantes.

Do total de inscritos na Paraíba em 2026, aproximadamente 102 mil tiveram direito à inscrição gratuita, enquanto 38,7 mil são pagantes.

Em todo o Brasil, o Enem reúne mais de 5 milhões de inscritos. Desse total, cerca de 3,4 milhões tiveram a inscrição gratuita e 1,6 milhão pagou a taxa para participar do exame.

As provas do Enem 2026 serão aplicadas nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro, em dois domingos consecutivos.

Nos dois dias, os portões dos locais de prova serão abertos às 12h e fechados às 13h, seguindo o horário de Brasília. O início da aplicação está previsto para as 13h30.

No primeiro dia, os participantes farão as provas de Linguagens, Códigos e suas Tecnologias, Redação e Ciências Humanas e suas Tecnologias. A duração será de cinco horas e 30 minutos.

Já no segundo domingo, serão aplicadas as provas de Ciências da Natureza e suas Tecnologias e Matemática e suas Tecnologias, com duração de cinco horas.

Os participantes devem ficar atentos aos horários e às datas de aplicação para evitar atrasos e possíveis impedimentos de entrada nos locais de prova.

articles.summary: Bilhetes premiados foram registrados em 13 municípios piauienses. Prêmio principal acumulou e está estimado em R$ 46 milhões.
articles.body:
Vinte e oito apostas feitas no Piauí acertaram quatro números da Mega-Sena no concurso 3.080, sorteado neste domingo (1º). Os bilhetes premiados foram registrados em 13 municípios do estado, incluindo a capital Teresina .

O prêmio para as apostas que acertassem as seis dezenas era de R$ 40,7 milhões. No entanto, ninguém levou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou para R$ 46 milhões.

As dezenas sorteadas foram: 13 - 17 - 28 - 29 - 39 - 58

As apostas piauienses premiadas acertaram quatro dezenas e receberam R$ 514,10 cada. Uma das apostas foi um bolão de 18 cotas em Teresina. Outra aposta de Teresina foi feita com 7 números, gerando prêmio maior de R$ 1.542,30.

Veja as cidades do Piauí com apostas premiadas

No país, 29 apostas acertaram cinco números e receberam R$ 38.878,66. Outras 3.133 apostas acertaram quatro dezenas, com prêmio de R$ 514,10 cada.

A aposta simples da Mega-Sena custa R$ 6. Os jogos podem ser feitos em casas lotéricas ou pelos canais digitais da Caixa Econômica Federal, no site e no aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

Em regra, as apostas podem ser registradas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) nos dias de sorteio. Os bolões digitais podem ser comprados até as 20h30 pelos canais eletrônicos.

Nos sorteios realizados aos domingos, as apostas simples podem ser feitas até as 22h do sábado anterior nas lotéricas, no Portal Loterias Caixa e no aplicativo. Os bolões eletrônicos podem ser comprados até as 10h45 de domingo, 15 minutos antes do sorteio.

As apostas pela internet podem ser pagas por Pix, cartão de crédito ou internet banking, no caso de correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

Bilhetes da Mega-Sena, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

Segundo a Caixa Econômica Federal, a chance de acertar as seis dezenas com uma aposta simples, de seis números, é de uma em 50.063.860.

Já uma aposta com 20 dezenas, o limite máximo permitido, tem uma chance em 1.292 de ganhar o prêmio principal. Nesse caso, o jogo custa R$ 232.560.

articles.title: Homem morre afogado em represa na zona rural de Araçuaí | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima estava com familiares quando decidiu nadar na represa de uma fazenda, na comunidade de Lagoa dos Patos. Corpo foi encontrado a cerca de cinco metros de profundidade.
articles.summary: Vítima estava com familiares quando decidiu nadar na represa de uma fazenda, na comunidade de Lagoa dos Patos. Corpo foi encontrado a cerca de cinco metros de profundidade.
articles.body:
Homem morre afogado em represa na zona rural de Araçuaí — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Um homem de aproximadamente 39 anos morreu afogado na tarde deste sábado (31) em uma represa na zona rural de Araçuaí , no Vale do Jequitinhonha. O acidente aconteceu na comunidade de Lagoa dos Patos.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a vítima estava acompanhada de familiares quando decidiu nadar na represa. Por motivos ainda desconhecidos, ele se afogou e desapareceu na água.

Os militares foram acionados e iniciaram as buscas submersas. O corpo foi localizado a cerca de cinco metros de profundidade e a pouco mais de 20 metros da margem.

Após a retirada da água, o corpo foi entregue à funerária responsável pelos procedimentos seguintes.

articles.title: O que são as eleições de meio de mandato e o que Trump arrisca? | G1
articles.standfirst: Os eleitores dos EUA irão às urnas em 3 de novembro em uma votação que poderá ter um grande impacto na presidência de Donald Trump.
articles.summary: Os eleitores dos EUA irão às urnas em 3 de novembro em uma votação que poderá ter um grande impacto na presidência de Donald Trump.
articles.body:
Faltam poucos dias para as eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos , as midterms, quando os eleitores participarão de uma votação que poderá ter um grande impacto no restante do mandato do presidente Donald Trump — previsto para terminar em janeiro de 2029.

Em 3 de novembro, os americanos escolherão os membros do Congresso, que é composto por duas casas: a Câmara dos Representantes e o Senado.

As eleições acontecem a cada dois anos e, quando ocorrem no meio do mandato de quatro anos do presidente, são chamadas de eleições de meio de mandato.

Uma das principais tarefas do Congresso é criar e aprovar leis federais, que são aplicadas em todo o país.

O resultado das eleições de meio de mandato decidirá qual partido político — os republicanos da sigla de Trump ou os democratas, da oposição — controlará o Congresso e quão fácil será para o presidente executar seus planos.

Os resultados também são vistos como uma métrica da satisfação da população americana com o desempenho do presidente até o momento.

Em 3 de novembro, os americanos escolherão os membros do Congresso, que é composto por duas casas: a Câmara dos Representantes e o Senado. — Foto: BBC

Todos os 435 membros da Câmara dos Representantes, a câmara baixa do Congresso, serão eleitos. Eles cumprem mandatos fixos de dois anos. A Câmara é geralmente o local onde as propostas de lei são apresentadas e debatidas.

Enquanto isso, 35 das 100 cadeiras do Senado, a câmara alta, também estarão em disputa. Os senadores têm mandatos de seis anos. Entre outras funções, eles aprovam ou vetam projetos de lei que vieram da Câmara dos Deputados.

No mesmo dia, eleitores em grande parte dos EUA também escolherão políticos em nível estadual. As eleições para governador na Califórnia, Flórida, Geórgia e Michigan estão entre as que despertam mais atenção.

Quais pautas estão sendo mais debatidas nessa eleição?

A economia dos EUA está na mente de muitos americanos que enfrentam os preços dos combustíveis, alimentos, cuidados com a saúde e com a habitação.

A inflação permanece acima da meta almejada pelo Federal Reserve (o banco central) dos EUA , em parte devido à guerra que os EUA e Israel iniciaram com o Irã em fevereiro.

Os democratas argumentam que as tarifas impostas por Trump sobre vários países também aumentaram os preços para os americanos.

A imigração é outra questão crucial. Os republicanos afirmam que Trump cumpriu uma importante promessa de campanha de 2024 ao reforçar a segurança na fronteira e lançar uma forte repressão — e frequentemente controversa — à imigração ilegal.

A preocupação com a inteligência artificial (IA) tornou-se mais urgente nas últimas semanas. Políticos de alto escalão de ambos os partidos concordaram com a necessidade de regulamentá-la, opondo-se a Trump, que rejeita propostas de leis para controlar o desenvolvimento dessa tecnologia.

As midterms serão um último veredito dos eleitores sobre o governo Trump antes que este termine. — Foto: Reuters via BBC

O legislativo é um dos três poderes do Estado, juntamente com o Executivo (representado a nível federal pela presidência) e o judiciário. O controle sobre ele é importante para a elaboração de leis.

Tanto a Câmara dos Representantes quanto o Senado são atualmente controlados pelo Partido Republicano. Mas sua maioria é pequena. Eles têm 218 cadeiras na Câmara, que é o número mínimo necessário para controlá-la, mais um independente que vota com eles.

No Senado, eles têm 53 cadeiras. A câmara alta só mudará de mãos se os democratas conquistarem pelo menos 51 cadeiras, o que superaria o voto de desempate do vice-presidente — atualmente republicano — caso ambos os lados obtenham 50 cadeiras.

Se os democratas da oposição recuperarem o controle de pelo menos uma das casas legislativas, terão o poder de apresentar suas próprias leis para votação.

O democrata Josh Turek e a republicana Ashley Hinson estão em uma disputa acirrada pela vaga no Senado pelo estado de Iowa. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

No passado, os eleitores tendiam a "punir" o partido do presidente e votar contra ele.

Pesquisas recentes mostram que Trump tem um baixo índice de aprovação. Ele iniciou seu segundo mandato com aprovação de pouco mais de 50% da população, segundo o site de pesquisas Silver Bulletin. No início de outubro, esse índice era mais baixo, em torno de 37%. Enquanto isso, 61% o desaprovavam.

Mas nem todas as cadeiras em cada casa legislativa serão de fato disputadas. Algumas têm apostas seguras, em alguns casos para republicanos e em outros para democratas.

A CBS News, parceira da BBC nos EUA, identificou dez disputas para o Senado que merecem atenção, em estados como Iowa e New Hampshire; e 42 disputas para a Câmara dos Representantes, em estados como Arizona e Ohio.

A votação deste ano é mais imprevisível devido a uma disputa entre os dois partidos sobre a forma como os distritos eleitorais na Câmara dos Representantes são definidos.

Os republicanos tentaram obter vantagem criando mapas eleitorais mais favoráveis em certos estados, e os democratas seguiram o exemplo.

O que essa eleição significa para Trump?

As midterms serão um último veredito dos eleitores sobre o governo Trump antes que este termine, explica Anthony Zurcher, correspondente da BBC na América do Norte.

Se os democratas vencerem a Câmara ou o Senado, Trump terá dificuldades para aprovar qualquer lei no Congresso — embora o republicano já tenha demonstrado a disposição de promover sua agenda através de ordens executivas, que não precisam do Congresso.

Mas o controle democrata de qualquer uma das casas legislativas facilitaria o uso de comissões para investigar aspectos do mandato de Trump. Parlamentares poderiam convocar funcionários públicos para depor e solicitar documentos.

Poderão ser alvo de escrutínio acusações de corrupção, o polêmico novo salão de baile da Casa Branca e as táticas do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega (ICE, na sigla em inglês).

Há também um debate dentro do Partido Democrata sobre se deve ou não iniciar um processo de impeachment contra Trump, apresentando acusações no Congresso que serviriam de base para um julgamento político, e não criminal.

Se conseguirem controle do Senado, os democratas poderiam dificultar a nomeação por Trump de juízes e cargos de alto escalão, incluindo para a Suprema Corte.

Mas, se o Partido Republicano mantiver o controle do Congresso, Trump poderá dar continuidade, com mais facilidade, aos seus planos no restante do seu mandato.

O que a eleição pode indicar sobre 2028?

O nome do presidente não consta na cédula eleitoral durante as eleições de meio de mandato, embora Trump tenha pedido que os eleitores finjam que consta, como forma de endossar seu governo até o momento.

Independente do resultado, é provável que os analistas o utilizem com termômetro de como os eleitores se sentem em relação aos rumos do país sob a liderança de Trump.

O republicano não pode se candidatar à presidência pela terceira vez, já que, segundo a Constituição, uma pessoa não poder exercer mais do que dois mandatos de presidente nos EUA.

Após as eleições de meio de mandato, podemos esperar que comecem as especulações sobre quem poderá ser seu sucessor como candidato republicano à presidência em 2028 — e quem poderá competir contra ele pelo Partido Democrata.

articles.summary: Turma do Pagode se apresenta no Recinto de Exposições de São José do Rio Preto com sucessos de 30 anos de carreira e faixas do projeto inédito Turma Futebol Clube.
articles.body:
Em conjunto com Sorriso Maroto e Ferrugem, o grupo Turma do Pagode desembarca em São José do Rio Preto (SP) neste domingo (1º) para uma apresentação que promete os clássicos da carreira e muito pagode no Recinto de Exposições. Para o grupo, voltar ao interior paulista é uma oportunidade de reencontrar fãs que acompanham a trajetória da banda há anos.

🎶 Turma do Pagode é formado por Leiz, que comanda o tantã e vocal ; Caramelo, responsável pelo banjo e vocal ; Rubinho, que fica com o pandeiro ; Tiago e Neni tocam a percussão ; Marcelinho no cavaquinho ; Leandro Filé toca o violão e Fabiano comanda o surdo .

Ao g1 , os integrantes da banda, destacaram a importância de dividir a programação com artistas que também ajudaram a construir a história do pagode brasileiro e destacaram o momento de força do gênero no país.

O grupo também comentou a relação construída com o público do interior paulista ao longo das últimas décadas. Segundo os integrantes, as apresentações na região são marcadas pelo reencontro com fãs que acompanham a carreira desde os primeiros sucessos.

"O público do interior de São Paulo sempre nos recebe com muito carinho. Uma das coisas mais marcantes dessa trajetória é perceber o quanto as nossas músicas fazem parte da vida das pessoas, acompanhando histórias de amor, amizades e diferentes momentos. Voltar à região é sempre uma oportunidade de renovar esse carinho e criar novas memórias com quem acompanha o nosso trabalho", pontuaram os músicos.

Com mais de 30 anos de carreira, a grupo Turma do Pagode chega ao evento com com músicas que marcaram sua trajetória e, além dos sucessos conhecidos pelo público, faixas do projeto mais recente, "Turma Futebol Clube".

Com a promessa de fazer o público cantar desde a abertura dos portões, programada para 15h, os músicos desejam transformar a noite em uma grande celebração do gênero.

"Vamos subir ao palco com muita vontade de fazer todo mundo cantar do começo ao fim e transformar essa noite em uma grande celebração do pagode”, finaliza a banda.

articles.title: Watch: NASA’s pencil-thin X-59 supersonic jet spotted flying across US skies
articles.summary: NASA’s pencil-thin X-59 experimental supersonic jet was captured flying over the United States on Wednesday, exactly one year after its maiden flight, as
articles.body: NASA’s pencil-thin X-59 experimental supersonic jet was captured flying over the United States on Wednesday, exactly one year after its maiden flight, as the aircraft began a cross-country journey from California to Florida.Videos of the distinctive aircraft have since surfaced on social media, drawing attention to the milestone. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman responded to one such video on X, writing: “Great catch... X-59 making her way to @NASAKennedy”.The aircraft was en route to NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida when it was spotted by people across the US. Videos of the unusual-looking jet were subsequently widely shared on X, drawing attention to its distinctive pencil-thin design. Its journey comes as the space agency marks a year of flight testing for the experimental aircraft, which is the centrepiece of its Quesst mission.The aircraft traveled escorted by an F-15, an F/A-18 and a Gulfstream C-20.NASA Aeronautics also marked the anniversary in a post on X, saying, “One year. New heights. Faster speeds. Since its first flight on Oct. 28, 2025, NASA's X-59 has continued pushing the boundaries of aviation. See how far we've come in just one year!”The agency shared a comparison of the aircraft’s performance on its first flight and one year later. On October 28, 2025, the X-59 reached an altitude of 12,000 feet, clocked a speed of 230 mph and remained airborne for 67 minutes. It had completed just one flight at the time.By October 28, 2026, the aircraft had reached a maximum altitude of 56,000 feet and a top speed of Mach 1.53. Its longest flight lasted 102 minutes, while its flight count had risen to 41, according to the figures shared by NASA Aeronautics.What makes NASA’s X-59 different?According to NASA, the X-59 is 99.7 feet long and 29.5 feet wide. Its most striking feature is its exceptionally long, narrow nose, which accounts for almost a third of the aircraft’s length. The shape is designed to distribute the shock waves generated during supersonic flight, preventing them from merging into the loud sonic boom commonly heard on the ground.The aircraft is powered by a single engine mounted on top of its fuselage. NASA says this positioning directs engine noise upwards, while the aircraft’s smooth underside helps prevent shock waves from combining.The cockpit is positioned almost halfway along the aircraft and has no conventional forward-facing window. Instead, pilots use NASA’s external vision system, which combines cameras and high-resolution displays to provide a view ahead and below the aircraft.NASA designed the X-59 to fly at Mach 1.4, or approximately 925 mph, at an altitude of 55,000 feet. It is an experimental research aircraft, not a prototype passenger plane, and will never carry passengers.NASA said the X-59’s first flight, piloted by test pilot Nils Larson, took place from the Lockheed Martin Skunk Works assembly site in Palmdale, California, to the agency’s Armstrong Flight Research Center. The initial flight focused on low-speed and low-altitude systems checks.The aircraft is not a prototype for a passenger airliner and will not carry passengers. NASA plans to use it to gather data on the sound generated during supersonic flight and residents’ responses when it flies over selected US communities.NASA said the programme will now move towards acoustic validation, studying the sound produced by the aircraft. articles.title: Woman rescues an injured queen bumblebee, helps her recover and creates a sheltered space for her; 100 days later, Phoebee has become an online sensation
articles.summary: We hear rescue stories every day. A dog pulled from a flooded ditch. A cat coaxed out from behind a fridge.
articles.body: We hear rescue stories every day. A dog pulled from a flooded ditch. A cat coaxed out from behind a fridge. But how often have you heard about a bumblebee with a broken wing?Gilly McArthur found one lying in the sun beside a road. She took it home, made it a bed of flowers and expected it wouldn’t last the day. Instead, the bumblebee now climbs McArthur’s arm, works her way around the back of her neck and disappears into her hair. The woman named the queen bee ‘Phoebee’, and strangers from around the world are obsessed with her.“I couldn’t leave her by the roadside. So I brought her home and made her a bed of flowers. I thought she’d be dead in a day or so,” McArthur told The Guardian, describing the extraordinary rescue. Contrary to McArthur’s fears, Phoebee survived and also became an internet celebrity.An unexpected travel partnerMcArthur was due to leave on a week-long sailing trip shortly after the rescue. She couldn’t leave the bee behind, so she brought Phoebee along. The woman posted about their voyage together on Instagram. "Phoebee is now at sea. It’s been nearly a month since I found her struggling on a hot concrete pavement in my town, unable to fly because one of her wings had been lost; well, it's now a postcard from us on the West Coast of Scotland. When I picked her I hadn't expected her to last this long!" she wrote on Instagram in August.The next morning, McArthur woke to messages from around the world. People wrote about bumblebees they had rescued, butterflies they had nursed and small creatures they had tried to save. The stories kept flooding in.McArthur is moved by the response but still a little puzzled by it. “I think it might be because the world is in such a polycrisis at the moment, and everyone is wanting to pull back to something authentic and kind,” she told the newspaper. “Perhaps Phoebee reminds people of a time when bumblebees were more prolific, in a world that isn’t on fire: lots of the messages said the videos helped them feel more grounded in a world where the algorithms are usually so grounded in clickbait and violence.”100 days of PhoebeeOn 24 October, McArthur posted a collage video of Phoebee, celebrating 100 days since the rescue. She also shared how the experience had been ‘weird’ yet eventful. “Sure, it's a bit weird, but in this world that we seem to be racing through and destroying at great speed, these small interactions of wonder, and truly observing something tiny and perfectly designed for life, can pack a lot of punch.”McArthur also spoke about her familiarity with bumblebees. “I've a bit of history with bumblebees, rescuing them on swims, popping them onto my head for an easy swim back to shore, so it probably wasn't too surprising that in the end, one would find me, or me it, for this sort of slice of life. Too much to say in a post about this and the wider observations that the bee is teaching me, so I'd better keep writing and see where it lands!” she wrote on Instagram.Over these days, McArthur also observed some of Phoebee’s unique traits. “She’s fascinating: she spends a lot of time cleaning herself like a cat. And I could watch her putting her long tongue out and getting the nectar out of the flowers for hours.”Britain has 24 species of bumblebee and more than 240 species of solitary bee. Most bumblebees live for only a year. Newly mated queens are the exception, hibernating in autumn and emerging in spring to start colonies of their own. Phoebee has not mated, so her future is uncertain.Andy Benson, of the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, is equally bemused by Phoebee. In his view, Phoebee had some natural advantages. She is a buff-tailed bumblebee, one of the biggest and fluffiest of the British species, and she is a queen, which he described as “the biggest and fluffiest of them all”. He praised McArthur’s compassion. “A third of British wild bees and hoverflies are in decline and a quarter of European species are at risk of extinction because of the loss of their natural habitat, climate change and bee-killing pesticides,” he says.The stakes are practical as well as ecological. Pollinators help produce roughly one in three mouthfuls of food, and crops that rely on them, including apples, beans, squashes and almonds, are worth far more than those that do not.Benson suggests giving such bees a home, not in your home, but in your garden. Plant a few flowers in a garden, a balcony box or a patch of earth, and hundreds of bees can find something to eat. Nobody needs to bring one home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party in Chandler's Ford
articles.summary: Hampshire Police believes an unknown group gained entry to the party at an address in Chandler's Ford.
articles.body:
Five teenagers have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party, police have said.

Officers were called to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, near Eastleigh, shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday.

The injured teens - three boys aged 16 and two aged 17 - were taken to hospital.

Hampshire Police said it believes an unknown group gained entry to a party at an address on Park Road before the stabbings.

The force has appealed for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward.

A police cordon remained in place on Sunday while officers continue their investigation.

Senior investigating officer Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie acknowledged the impact on local residents and thanked the community for its patience.

Earlier, an eyewitness told the BBC ambulances and an air ambulance had attended.

Another eyewitness said they saw someone running out of the house involved, shouting that he had been stabbed and that he was being chased by two people.

In a post on X on Sunday, Eastleigh MP Liz Jarvis said: "My thoughts are with the victims and their families and all those affected by the incident in Chandler's Ford last night, and my thanks go to our local police and emergency services for their prompt response.

"It's important not to speculate or share unverified information."

articles.title: More than 50 million votes cast in US midterm elections: What does it mean?
articles.summary: A record number of early votes is cast as both parties campaign before Tuesday’s polls.
articles.body:
Early voting has surged in the 2026 United States midterm elections with more than 50 million Americans casting their ballots as of Sunday, according to an analysis by the University of Florida.

Most of the 50 states allow early in-person voting while all of them allow mail-in voting. About 23 million people voted through mail-in ballots, which President Donald Trump unsuccessfully tried to curb before the elections.

With two days left to go before Election Day on Tuesday, support for Democrats was 51.5 percent and for Republicans 43.1 percent, the latest national polls suggested.

The president’s tariff policy and his decision to launch a war with Israel on Iran are hurting his Republican Party. Both have been blamed for contributing to a cost-of-living crisis.

Why are so many Americans voting early? How does it work?

Early voting gives US citizens a chance to cast their ballots before Election Day.

According to the US government, people may vote early in person in most states by visiting designated polling stations. All states offer vote-by-mail options, in which registered voters may receive and return ballots by Election Day by mail.

The number of states offering options to vote in person before November expanded from 24 in 2000 to 47 in 2026, plus Washington, DC. But early-voting periods, eligibility requirements and procedures vary widely by state.

This year, out of about 210 million registered voters, 53.14 million had voted early as of 6:56am East Coast time (11:56 GMT) on Sunday , according to the University of Florida analysis. This includes 29 million in-person votes and 23 million mail-in ballots.

In the 2022 midterm elections, 46 million people had voted early.

Early voting enthusiasm has been higher among Democrats this year with more than 11 million registered Democrats having voted early, compared with about 8 million registered Republicans, according to the university’s analysis.

Which states have seen a surge in early votes?

Early voting has particularly surged in the state of Texas, a key battleground, where more than 7 million people have already voted early. This is over 1.5 million more than voted early in the 2022 midterms, according to the University of Florida analysis.

According to an Associated Press polling analysis, in South Carolina, where Trump won by nearly 18 percentage points in 2024, early voting has surged 83 percent compared with the same point in 2022. The state has open races for governor and US Senate this year.

In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces Democratic Methodist minister Adam Hamilton, early voting has increased 34 percent with roughly 83,000 more ballots cast than at the same point four years ago, AP reported.

In Maine, where Republican Senator Susan Collins faces Democratic former state Senate President Troy Jackson, early voting is up 44 percent. Michigan has also recorded roughly 409,000 more early votes than at the same point in 2022, a 32 percent increase.

According to the University of Maryland’s Center for Democracy and Civic Engagement (CDCE), there are many reasons why Americans are voting early.

This could be because “some voters find early voting to be more logistically convenient than Election Day voting” or have been “mobilised” to vote early, it said.

“Many voters report voting early because of anxiety about the election or a feeling of wanting to ‘get it over with’ or ‘cross it off their list’ as soon as possible,” the CDCE said.

The centre added that some voters choose to vote early for social or cultural reasons. It noted how efforts like “Parties at the Polls” and community celebrations of voting “try to create a more celebratory environment at certain voting locations, especially during early in-person voting”.

While early turnout figures don’t show which candidates voters have chosen or what the final results will be, Democratic political strategist Celinda Lake told Al Jazeera this past week that many voters were looking for change.

“You got a lot of voters who say, ‘I’m going to do a Hail Mary for change, but I hope you do something,’” she said.

“We all just really want a better future for everyone, especially like the next generation,” one young voter told Al Jazeera.

Another young voter pointed to social media as a reason for the increased interest in the election. “Definitely social media. Social media and the media have put voting in the limelight,” the voter told Al Jazeera.

What has Trump said about mail-in voting?

Trump has repeatedly cast doubt on the security of mail-in voting, which enables people to vote early by mail. Trump, who himself has repeatedly voted by mail, cited debunked claims of widespread election fraud associated with it.

Mail-in ballots, which have been in place for decades, have been found to increase voter turnout and currently account for a third of all votes cast in the US.

State and county officials in eight states send ballots to the homes of all registered voters, who then mail them back before a deadline. The rest of the states send ballots only to the registered voters who request them. Voters may return the ballots through official election drop boxes. In some states, the ballots have to reach the voting centre by Election Day while in others, ballots postmarked by Election Day but received after it may still be counted.

Eight states, several of them Democratic-leaning – California, Colorado, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Vermont and Washington – as well as the District of Columbia allow all elections to be conducted entirely by mail.

Others allow smaller elections to be conducted by mail.

Trump has falsely blamed his 2020 presidential election loss on mail-in voting fraud. He and his supporters also opposed changes made during the COVID-19 pandemic to expand mail-in voting.

In March, Trump signed an executive order directing the US Postal Service to take control of mail-in voting by designing new envelopes with special barcodes that would allow the federal government to ensure ballots are only from eligible voters.

For the midterms, that move would have forced all states to adopt a uniform envelope style in a short time.

Democrats and activists challenged the order in several courts, resulting in a series of back-and-forth rulings from May to August.

Last month, however, the Supreme Court rejected Trump’s bid to require the mail-in voting restrictions before this month’s elections.

articles.title: Princess Catherine’s sister Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews ordered to demolish unauthorised car park at £15.5 million estate; neighbours raise concerns over construction without consultation
articles.summary: Pippa Middleton and her hedge fund manager husband, James Matthews, have been ordered to remove a car park they built on their sprawling country estate
articles.body: Pippa Middleton and her hedge fund manager husband, James Matthews, have been ordered to remove a car park they built on their sprawling country estate without obtaining prior planning permission. The decision comes after a group of residents in the picturesque village of Kintbury raised objections with West Berkshire Council, claiming they had not been consulted before construction began last year.Pippa, the younger sister of Princess Catherine, and James own the land, which forms part of their £15.5 million, 145-acre Barton Court estate. The couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.Council rules car park development was visually intrusiveAccording to a report by The Times, the couple subsequently applied for retrospective planning permission for the anglers' car park, arguing that the sale of fishing rights along the River Kennet was a significant source of income that helped support the upkeep of the estate.However, West Berkshire Council rejected the proposal, concluding that the development was 'visually intrusive and urbanised' and had 'eroded a measure of the open and undeveloped rural character' of the North Wessex Downs. The couple have now been directed to remove the car park.The development reportedly involved laying approximately 400 square metres of agricultural hard standing across a meadow. The land was previously known among residents as the grazing ground of two heavy horses, Monty and Drummer, who lived there before the estate changed hands.Neighbours objected to construction without consultationThe car park drew considerable criticism from residents, who approached the council after noticing the construction. In objections submitted to the authorities, locals said they were 'shocked' by the development and questioned why the community had not been consulted before work began.Some residents also alleged that the car park had been created to move vehicles away from areas closer to the couple's home, thereby preserving the views around their property.One objector reportedly wrote: 'This application is to move unsightly parking out of sight of the applicants on entry to the Barton Court estate to the detriment of the residents and the heritage of Kintbury.'Another resident highlighted concerns about the location, traffic congestion and the potential impact on the area's heritage, requesting that the planning committee conduct a site inspection before reaching a decision.Planners also raised concerns about the absence of mitigation measures to protect the River Kennet from potential adverse environmental impacts.Pippa Middleton and James Matthews' previous dispute with localsThis is not the first time Pippa and James have found themselves at odds with residents since moving to Barton Court. The couple previously faced opposition after restricting public access to Mill Lane, a route that runs through their estate and had reportedly been used by local dog walkers and ramblers for years.The Grade I-listed Barton Court, situated along the River Kennet near Kintbury, was previously owned by late retail tycoon Sir Terence Conran, who had allowed members of the public to use the lane.However, after Pippa and James moved into the property with their three children, Arthur, Grace and Rose, in 2022, they installed an electric gate to restrict access. Signs reading 'Private: No Public Access' and 'No Trespassing' also appeared around the estate.The move prompted 35 residents, supported by the Ramblers Association, to approach West Berkshire Council, seeking to have Mill Lane officially recognised as a public right of way.A Planning Inspectorate inquiry into the dispute began at the village hall in May. James Matthews also attended the proceedings, where he reportedly argued that the family's security and privacy concerns should be taken into consideration.You use AI every day. articles.title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
articles.summary: More than 4,000 people have been arrested for supporting the group since it was proscribed in July 2025.
articles.body:
More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.

Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."

The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made. The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".

At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.

The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation , after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.

The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.

Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine."

In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.

Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon - had travelled from Cumbria to participate. He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".

"I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.

David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".

Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".

According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026. Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.

The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.

Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.

Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.

articles.title: A 14-year-old Indiana girl started selling homemade slime to pay for a school trip; nine days later, she had met her fundraising goal, and within a month, her tiny business had drawn over 8 million views online
articles.summary: A 14-year-old girl from Indiana, United States, who started a small business to pay for a school trip has gained more than 30,000 social media followers
articles.body: A 14-year-old girl from Indiana, United States, who started a small business to pay for a school trip has gained more than 30,000 social media followers and over eight million online views in less than a month.Lexi Long, an eighth-grade student at Schmucker Middle School, began selling slime and squishy toys on October 1, to raise money for a class visit to Washington, DC, WNDU reported. She collected the required amount within nine days but continued selling her creations as more people began showing interest in her products.For Lexi, the idea came from something she had enjoyed since childhood. She liked making things with her hands, particularly slime and other craft items. When she needed money for the school trip, she decided to use that interest to earn it herself.The trip was something she had heard about for years. Students at her school knew that eighth graders had an opportunity to visit Washington, DC, and Lexi wanted to be part of it and pay for it herself.Speaking to local television station WNDU, Lexi explained why the trip mattered to her. "People talk about this in elementary school, like 'Eighth grade you get to go and all that stuff,'" she said. "So, I really wanted to get to go," she added.Lexi started selling handmade items at age fourAlthough her latest business has attracted considerable attention, Lexi was already familiar with making and selling things.When she was four, she wanted to travel to Chicago and buy an American Girl doll. To raise money, she began creating accessories for the dolls and selling them.That early experience was similar to what she did this October. Both times, she had a trip in mind and decided to earn money by making something herself. "I guess I kind of start businesses when I have a trip to go on," she told WNDU.Her mother, Jennifer Long, said Lexi had always shown an interest in working towards the things she wanted. "A lot of kids, in the teen years, just kind of want things given to them. And Lexi's never been that kind of kid," Jennifer said. "She's always been a go-getter," she added.This time, Lexi chose slime and squishy toys because they were already among her favourite activities. She had played with slime from a young age and enjoyed experimenting with craft projects."I just think it's a fun way to express yourself. I think that doing crafts and making stuff is really fun," she said.School trip target achieved in just nine daysLexi officially began her business on October 1. Her first priority was to earn enough money for the Washington trip, and she started taking her products to sales events.She did not have to wait long to reach her target. At her second event, just nine days after starting the business, she had raised the amount needed for the visit.However, she decided to continue selling rather than stop after meeting her original goal. Her products began appearing at community events and local businesses, bringing her into contact with more customers. One of the places where she sells her creations is Urban Swirl & Scoop, a self-service frozen yoghurt shop.The shop's owner, Chrissy Harper, saw a connection between the way customers served themselves frozen yoghurt and the activity offered through Lexi's products. "We are a self-serve frozen yogurt place, so I thought a self-serve squishy place would be a win-win," Harper told WNDU.The products have attracted customers of different ages. Harper recalled that even football players from the University of Notre Dame had taken part in making squishies at the shop."We even had the Notre Dame football players in here- big old guys, over at this bar making squishies. So, it's for any age," she said.Videos of products get eight million viewsWhile Lexi was meeting customers at local events, her business was also gaining attention on social media. She created a Facebook page for Slime & Squish on October 1. By October 24, the page had attracted more than 21,000 followers, while videos of her products had received over six million combined views.That same day, she displayed her creations at the Century Center in South Bend, Indiana, giving visitors another opportunity to see what she was selling.The online audience continued to grow over the following days. By October 30, Lexi had crossed 30,000 followers and eight million views.In an earlier interview with the station, Lexi said she enjoyed being able to share her interest in crafts with others. "I have always played with slime since I was a little kid and I love doing crafts stuff like that," she said. "So being able to like share what I like to do with everybody else is really nice, and I really enjoy doing it," she added.What Lexi hopes other children will learnHaving started her first small venture at four and another at 14, Lexi now wants other young people to feel confident about trying their own ideas. "Even if you think people won't like it, I guarantee you there's someone out there that will like what you do," she said.She also encouraged children not to give up on something simply because it appears difficult. "Whatever you put your mind to, you can do it. Even if you think you can't, you really can," she said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Cops raid West Virginia frat houses in hazing probe as growing crackdown should be ‘wake-up call’: expert
articles.summary: Police served search warrants at West Virginia University's Lambda Chi Alpha and Pi Kappa Alpha houses amid fraternity hazing investigations.
articles.body: In the latest in a slew of fraternity hazing investigations nationwide, law enforcement agencies are poring over evidence taken from the Lambda Chi Alpha fraternity house at West Virginia University. On Oct. 26, blaring music pounded as hundreds of shouting bystanders lined the street and nearby properties of the multi-level, brick, frat house on the Morgantown campus. Meanwhile, officers with the campus and local police department, armed with a search warrant tied to hazing allegations, stoically toted out bags and cases of evidence and loaded it into police cars. FOUR FRATERNITY PLEDGES ARRESTED ON HAZING ALLEGATIONS AFTER TEEN FORCED INTO TRUCK: COPS A little more than two weeks earlier on Oct. 9, the university placed the chapter on interim suspension after "anonymous allegations of hazing," a university spokeswoman told Fox News Digital. Search warrants also were served on Oct. 26 at the house for the school’s chapter of Pi Kappa Alpha, according to social media posts from WVU Safety and Wellness. LSU FRAT PLEDGES ALLEGEDLY WATERBOARDED, FORCED TO CHUG MILK IN HAZING RITUALS: REPORT That fraternity, commonly known as PIKE, also is under investigation for allegations of hazing. As of that date, the university’s PIKE organization had not been put on suspension by the university. New interest in long-standing ritual The two West Virginia University chapters are the latest fraternities under investigation in an influx of Greek life hazing probes across the country. Hazing involves requiring new or potential recruits to the military or college fraternities to perform strenuous, humiliating or dangerous tasks. FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS The uptick in law enforcement involvement nationwide doesn’t necessarily signal an increase in hazing, said Michael Ayalon, hazing prevention expert and CEO of Greek University. More likely is that there’s increased awareness about hazing, triggered by changes to federal law, Ayalon told Fox News Digital. MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY The Stop Campus Hazing Act passed in December 2024 with bipartisan support in Congress. It requires more transparency in hazing allegations across the country, Ayalon said. "We certainly are seeing increased visibility and scrutiny of hazing on college campuses, particularly as universities face greater expectations for transparency and accountability. DOZENS OF PLEDGES FOUND COVERED IN FOOD IN SWELTERING FRAT BASEMENT AS POLICE INVESTIGATE ALLEGED HAZING "With that transparency and accountability comes greater visibility." But more visibility doesn’t necessarily suggest more hazing is occurring now, he said. ARIZONA LAWMAKERS DEMAND INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION INTO ASU HOCKEY WORKOUT THAT LEFT PLAYER IN COMA Hazing always has been underreported, he said, due to fear of retaliation. ‘A wake-up call’ Fraternity members should recognize that public perception of fraternity life now is being affected by these investigations, he said. "The positive contributions of thousands of fraternity members can get overshadowed by allegations involving a handful of chapters," Ayalon said. "So every hazing incident makes it harder for the good chapters to go out and recruit more new members, makes it harder for alumni to defend the fraternity experience, and it makes it harder for universities that are working with these organizations." "For students, I think this is a wake-up call." Despite decades of education about the dangers of hazing traditions, national policy changes and tragic deaths, "some chapters continue to believe that hazing is a necessary part of earning membership," he said. It’s based on flawed thinking, he said. Members justify the abuse, he said, by telling themselves, "I had to go through it, so you have to go through it, too." Fraternity chapters promote the idea that hazing builds brotherhood and creates loyalty, he said. SEND US A TIP "But there is a profound difference between working through a meaningful challenge as equals and being humiliated or controlled by people who hold power over you." Historically, hazing methods have followed patterns based on the kind of fraternity of sorority involved, Ayalon said. GOT A TIP? Fraternities that are traditionally White, known as IFC fraternities, are known for forced alcohol consumption, he said. Eighty-two percent of hazing deaths involve forced alcohol consumption. In historically White sororities, hazing typically takes a different form, he said. In Panhellenic organizations, hazing looks like mental abuse—mean-girl behavior that ostracizes new female members. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL In historically Black fraternities and sororities of the National Pan-Hellenic Council (NPHC) —often called the Divine Nine—abuse may be physical or mental, Ayalon said. And some recent high-profile cases of hazing have involved drugs, he said. "West Virginia University takes seriously the safety and well-being of our students," a spokeswoman for West Virginia University said. articles.title: Israel election: When will government be formed, who will lead it?
articles.summary: President Herzog must tap candidate to form new government by November 11, with fraught negotiations likely to follow.
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his coalition’s parliamentary majority following legislative elections on October 27.

But a bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu also failed to win a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, leaving Israel without a clear path to a new government.

What’s ahead is likely weeks of political wrangling as Israel’s disparate factions weigh possible governing arrangements, including a unity government bringing rival factions together or a minority government reliant on outside support. If they fail to reach an agreement, Israel could head back to the polls.

What are the final results of Israel’s elections?

The pro-Netanyahu coalition won 53 seats:

A bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu won 48 seats:

That leaves all existing blocs short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, meaning some parties would have to realign or join forces across bloc lines to form a new government.

Israel’s election results must be officially certified and presented to President Isaac Herzog by November 4 .

The new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10 .

Herzog must task one incoming Knesset member with forming a new government by November 11 . He is expected to make his decision with input from party leaders, selecting the candidate he believes has the best chance of building a coalition.

The candidate commissioned by Herzog has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible extension of 14 days .

Who will Herzog nominate first to form a government?

He has not said yet, but the most likely candidates are Netanyahu or former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar party received the most votes in the opposition bloc.

According to Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth media, Eisenkot may have an edge over Netanyahu as some Arab-led parties consider endorsing him in a bid to oust Netanyahu.

Herzog, for his part, has urged Israeli politicians to move away from rigid partisan stances and look for “creative solutions” that will lead to a new government and avoid a second round of elections.

Before the election, Herzog said he would do everything he could to spare the country another election cycle, even if that means pressing for a national unity government that brings together rivals Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

Could the opposition bloc join forces with Arab-led parties?

Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have previously ruled out partnering with the Arab-led parties .

Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak, however, has said he believes they “can change their mind”, arguing that Netanyahu would do in their position.

“If Netanyahu had a similar problem, he would immediately invite Mansour Abbas”, the leader of Ra’am and “give him the role of a minister of interior”, Barak told France 24 on Friday.

Abbas himself has signalled a willingness to work the opposition camp, saying Eisenkot’s conditions would not pose an obstacle for his party, according to Israel’s Channel 12.

Yousef Jabareen from the Arab-led Joint List has also said that his party is ready for the “ousting of the Netanyahu government”.

“The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership,” he wrote on X.

Even if Arab-led parties do not formally join the opposition’s coalition, they could prop it up from outside by helping it pass a confidence vote in the Knesset.

Raluca Ganea, co-founder of Israeli civil society group Zazim, told Al Jazeera that a coalition between the opposition bloc and the Arab-led parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel “is the only path forward for Israeli democracy as a whole”.

What happens if no one can form a government?

If Herzog’s first candidate fails to form a government within the 42 days, the Israeli president has the option of asking another Knesset member to try to do so within 28 days. If that candidate also fails, a majority of Knesset members could put forward a third candidate, who would have a final 14 days to try to assemble one.

Even without a coalition commanding at least 61 seats, a candidate could still try to form a minority government by relying on outside support from smaller parties, including Arab-led parties, or negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with alternating prime ministers.

If none of these options succeed and deadlock persists, the Knesset would be formally dissolved, and Israelis would return to the polls for another round of elections.

Those elections would have to be called within 90 days.

Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.

If the process drags out, that could leave Israel’s longest-serving prime minister in power for months more, even if he ultimately fails to become part of the next governing coalition.

articles.title: At least 6 shot near University of Delaware during Halloween celebrations
articles.summary: Six people were shot on Halloween night along a crowded stretch of Main Street in Newark, Delaware, sending people running for safety as police rushed to the scene.
articles.body: Six people were shot on Halloween night along a crowded stretch of Main Street in Newark, Delaware, sending people running for safety as police rushed to the scene. The shooting happened on the sidewalk along Main Street right after 11 p.m., across from Choate Street, near the University of Delaware. All six victims were taken to area hospitals for treatment. The university had sent out an emergency alert at 11:29 p.m. notifying the community of the incident and warning them to avoid the area. Witnesses said Main Street was packed with college students and others celebrating Halloween when gunshots rang out, triggering panic among the crowds. “People were running, screaming. They had helicopters in the sky flashing lights on people. The people were speeding down the road. It got chaotic like quick,” witness Jayden Ngalim said. Another witness, Nathaniel Davila, said he was standing nearby when he heard what sounded like popping noises. “I was right there on the corner and all we hear is like sharp pops. People, we’re thinking at first it’s the cars and then everyone starts running,” Davila said. Landon Singleton, who witnessed the aftermath of the shooting, said that he rushed to help after seeing multiple people lying wounded in the street. “I immediately just no second thought. I didn’t think of anything else. Didn’t even think about myself like my life. Anything. I just ran straight towards there just to help,” Singleton said. Singleton added that he noticed one young victim lying on his back, surrounded by friends who appeared unsure of what to do. Singleton said he immediately approached the victim, removed his shirt, folded it and pressed it against the gunshot wound. “He squeezed my hand, like his like last hope,” Singleton said. Singleton added, “It was very, very chaotic, very intense.” Main Street began reopening around 3 a.m. Sunday following the shooting. Newark police have not released information about the victims’ conditions or said whether anyone has been arrested. Police are asking anyone with photos or video of the incident to submit them through the department’s evidence portal. Anyone with additional information is asked to contact Detective Paige Klein at 302-366-7100, ext. 3480, or pklein@newark.de.us, or visit the department’s tips page.

articles.title: In 1699, a Ming royal descendant who became a Buddhist monk painted 12 leaves of birds and flowers; after passing through famous collectors and a 1991 auction, the album sold for about Rs 75 crore in 2026
articles.summary: Nature's longest affair is perhaps that between birds and flowers.
articles.body: Nature's longest affair is perhaps that between birds and flowers. The birds cling to the flowers, drinking their sweet nectar like a thirsty man who has finally found water in the desert. And all the flowers ask in return is that the birds carry their seeds far and wide, allowing new life to take root. It is a relationship that has existed for centuries, one that has inspired poets, painters and storytellers across cultures.Bada Shanren was one painter who found extraordinary beauty in this seemingly ordinary relationship. His subjects were often no more than birds perched on branches, flowers in bloom, fish swimming in ponds and rocks resting in an otherwise empty landscape. Yet, he captured their essence in a way few artists could.In the early spring of 1699, Bada Shanren painted Flowers and Birds, an album of twelve ink-on-paper leaves. At 73, he had reached the height of his artistic maturity. More than three centuries later, the album made headlines when it sold for HK$61.9 million (approximately Rs 75 crore) at Christie's Hong Kong on October 27, 2026. But the story of these twelve leaves begins much earlier, with a royal descendant who abandoned his former life to become a Buddhist monk.Who was Bada Shanren?Born Zhu Da in 1626 in Nanchang, in China's Jiangxi province, Bada Shanren belonged to a branch of the Ming imperial family. His childhood was steeped in art and literature, and he showed an early aptitude for poetry, painting and calligraphy. However, his life took a dramatic turn in 1644, when the Ming dynasty fell to the invading Manchu forces, bringing an end to nearly three centuries of imperial rule.As a member of the former royal house, Zhu Da faced an uncertain future under the new Qing dynasty. He sought refuge in a Buddhist monastery, where he lived as a monk for nearly three decades. Around 1680, he left the priesthood and returned to secular life, eventually establishing himself as a professional painter and calligrapher. It was during this period that he adopted the name Bada Shanren, under which he would become one of China's most distinctive artists.His paintings were often sparse, leaving large portions of the paper untouched. Flowers, branches, fish and birds emerged from a few deliberate brushstrokes, with the surrounding emptiness becoming as important as the subjects themselves. Beneath their seemingly uncomplicated appearance, however, his works carried a sense of melancholy, solitude and, at times, a quiet resistance to the world around him. His loyalty to the fallen Ming dynasty is also believed to have shaped some of the symbolism in his art.What was Flowers and Birds about?Created during his late Lotus Garden Period, Flowers and Birds brings together 12 individual compositions featuring the namesake, fish and rocks. Each leaf measures approximately 30.5 by 27.5 cm and is painted in ink on paper. Rather than filling the surface with intricate details, Bada allowed each subject to occupy its own space, making the simplest of compositions feel remarkably expressive.Among the subjects are plum blossoms, orchids, lotus flowers, bamboo, chrysanthemums, lilies and birds perched among branches. There are also depictions of a myna, an old tree and two birds. The compositions are held together by his distinctive brushwork, which shifts between delicate, almost fleeting strokes and darker, more assertive marks.Perhaps the most recognisable feature of Bada's bird paintings is their unusual eyes. Often turned upwards or positioned at an angle, their gaze gives the birds an almost human expression. They appear watchful, aloof and occasionally suspicious, as though observing the world without quite wishing to participate in it. It is a small detail, but one that gives these otherwise simple subjects an unmistakable personality.He highlights using the empty space itself. A bird does not need an elaborate landscape behind it, nor does a flower need a crowded garden to appear complete. The untouched paper becomes part of the composition, allowing the viewer to pause and look closer. This restraint, combined with his expressive brushwork, is what makes Bada's paintings so distinctive.Where is the painting now?The album's journey through the hands of collectors is almost as remarkable as the artwork itself. It was first recorded in the collection of Pan Zhengwei, a prominent Qing-dynasty collector, in his Record of Paintings and Calligraphy in the Tingfanlou Collection. Pan admired Bada's exquisite brushwork and ink effects, noting that the paintings were originally accompanied by ten additional leaves of calligraphy.The album subsequently passed through the collections of Wang Kemin and Zhang Zhiqin before entering the celebrated Dafengtang collection of Zhang Daqian, one of China's most renowned modern painters and collectors. It later belonged to Wang Fangyu, a Chinese art scholar and professor at Yale University, and his wife, Sum Wai. The couple assembled one of the most significant private collections of Bada Shanren's works.In 1990, Flowers and Birds was exhibited at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco as part of Master of the Lotus Garden: The Life and Art of Bada Shanren. It travelled to the Yale University Art Gallery in 1991, where it was also featured in the accompanying exhibition catalogue.That same year, the album appeared at Christie's New York's Fine Chinese Paintings and Calligraphy auction on November 23, as Lot 130. It subsequently passed through E&J Frankel Ltd in New York before being acquired by its next owner in 2020.Its latest appearance was at Christie's Hong Kong in October 2026, where it sold for HKD 61.9 million, more than five times its lowest estimate of HKD 12 million. The buyer has not been publicly identified, and the album is now understood to have entered another private collection.Three centuries after Bada Shanren first put brush to paper, his 12 leaves continue to travel, finding new admirers across generations. Perhaps that is the beauty of his work: he depicted ordinary things in an extraordinary manner through his paintings.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
